comment: Task T3.2 with the ESM-2 encoder UNFROZEN. Same dataset_v1, same pairwise architecture and same head hyperparameters as the frozen run t32-pairwise-a65bdee1b5ab, so the one difference is that all 33 transformer layers now receive gradients. Measured cost: 7,217 residues/s, 25.4 GB peak, about 1.63 h per epoch against 0.31 h frozen (reports/experiments/finetune_calibration.json).
comment_training: Both architectures use these same settings, which is what T3.2's 'under the same conditions' requires. max_tokens is a padded-residue budget rather than a batch size because chain lengths span 1 to 4128; accumulate_steps buys a larger effective batch without the memory of one.
comment_source_aware: T2.6's source-aware composite loss is off for T3.2 and on for T3.3. T3.2 trains on CATH alone, where every source mask is open, so the only thing source_aware would change is the shape of the residue objective -- it splits the 3-way cross-entropy into separate assignment and boundary terms. Turning it on here would make the T3.2 runs already in reports/experiments/ irreproducible from this file for no experimental gain. T3.3, which adds Pfam and TED, cannot run without it: those sources are silent about unannotated residues, and the T2.3 loss would read that silence as linker.
comment_accumulation: accumulate_steps is 1: at max_tokens 24000 a batch already holds ~86 chains, so accumulating gave an effective batch of ~344 and only ~570 optimiser steps per epoch. Memory is not the constraint at 40 GB, so the steps are worth more than the larger batch. Both architectures use the same value, as T3.2 requires.
comment_finetune: max_tokens drops from 24000 to 4096 because activations now have to be kept or recomputed; 4096 measured fastest at 25.4 GB of the 40 GB card, and 8192 risks OOM for roughly 10% more throughput. encoder_learning_rate is 1e-5 against the heads' 1e-3: a pretrained encoder at the heads' rate is destroyed in the first epoch. finetune_layers 0 means all 33 layers, which is what 'unfrozen' asks for; setting it to 8 trains the top eight for 0.86 h per epoch instead.
comment_budget: 20 epochs is about 33 GPU-hours. protocol.MAX_RUN_HOURS caps a single run at 8 h and protocol.BUDGET_GPU_HOURS caps T3.2 at 30, so this run will stop itself at the cap after roughly 5 epochs and record that it did. Fine-tuning usually peaks within a few epochs, so 5 is enough to see whether it helps; going further is a decision about the budget, not about the code.
